title: Learning to Decide with AI Assistance under Human-Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2605.12646v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: It is widely agreed that when AI models assist decision-makers in high-stakes domains by predicting an outcome of interest, they should communicate the confidence of their predictions. However, empirical evidence suggests that decision-makers often struggle to determine when to trust a prediction based solely on this communicated confidence. In this context, recent theoretical and empirical work suggests a positive correlation between the utility of AI-assisted decision-making and the degree of alignment between the AI confidence and the decision-makers' confidence in their own predictions. Crucially, these findings do not yet elucidate the extent to which this alignment influences the complexity of learning to make optimal decisions through repeated interactions. translated_title: 人机对齐条件下学习借助AI辅助进行决策
translated_abstract: 人们普遍认为，当AI模型通过预测感兴趣的结果来辅助高风险领域的决策者时，它应当传达其预测的置信度。然而，实证证据表明，决策者往往难以仅凭所传达的置信度来判断何时应当信任某个预测。在这一背景下，近期的理论与实证研究指出，AI辅助决策的效用与AI置信度和决策者对自身预测置信度之间的对齐程度呈正相关。至关重要的是，这些发现尚未阐明这种对齐究竟在多大程度上影响通过反复交互学习最优决策的复杂度。本文在二元预测与二元决策这一经典情形下研究该问题。我们首先证明该问题等价于一个双臂（老虎机）问题。
tldr: 本文揭示了AI置信度与人类对自身预测的置信度之间的对齐程度如何影响AI辅助决策中通过反复交互学习最优决策的复杂度，并将该学习问题归约为双臂老虎机问题。
en_tdlr: This paper shows how the alignment between AI confidence and decision-makers' confidence in their own predictions affects the complexity of learning to make optimal decisions through repeated interactions in AI-assisted decision-making, reducing the problem to a two-armed bandit.
